title: Adapter Capability Declaration Schema
description: A vendor-agnostic, versioned schema that every compute, LLM, storage, or routing adapter must satisfy to integrate with the Trust Harness.

why: Replacing the CC stand-in reconstruction with our authoritative, production-grade Adapter Capability Declaration Schema.

The stand-in treated this as an agent self-claim contract with policy thresholds, whereas our authoritative version is the strict, vendor-agnostic adapter specification required for real integrations in the Trust Harness.
Hardened to support precise ANFIS routing optimization metrics and secure fail-closed operational behaviors.

reconciled.why: Checked against main for the same kind of collision found in events.v1.json. All of GA's changes here are additive or strictly tightening (additionalProperties:false, currency, max_budget_limit_usd, routing_fail_behavior, an expanded failure_modes enum) except one real shape break: latency_class changes from a plain string enum (main) to a required object {classification, expected_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms} (this version). A grep of both repos' TypeScript for `latency_class` found no current consumer, so today's blast radius is zero -- kept as GA wrote it, flagged here so whoever wires the first real consumer picks the object shape deliberately rather than discovering the break at runtime.

usd_per_1k_input.description: The cost in USD per 1,000 input tokens.

usd_per_1k_output.description: The cost in USD per 1,000 output tokens.

fixed_overhead_usd.description: Flat connection or initiation overhead fee in USD per invocation.

max_budget_limit_usd.description: Maximum allowed cost ceiling per single invocation to prevent runaway billing loop defects.

latency_class.description: Quantitative and qualitative latency profile to support ANFIS routing optimization.

expected_latency_ms.description: Mean/expected response duration under nominal load conditions.

p95_latency_ms.description: 95th percentile latency cutoff threshold. The router will trigger timeout fallbacks exceeding this limit.

degradation_class.description: Rules governing degraded network states and fail-closed behaviors.

routing_fail_behavior.description: Routing lane fail-closed policy. 'fail_closed' is standard and mandatory for production-security lanes to prevent unmonitored silent bypasses.

fallback_supported.description: Whether the adapter can seamlessly fail over to a local/sibling node without throwing a fatal exception.

failure_modes.description: Explicit list of standard failure signatures the adapter can return, allowing the router to execute precise recovery steps.
